title: Sales Tax, Income Tax and Personal Budgets
seo_title: Grade 7 Sales Tax, Income Tax and Budget Worksheets (TEKS 7.13, STAAR)
short_title: Sales Tax, Income Tax and Budgets
standard_text: 7.13A calculate the sales tax for a given purchase and calculate income tax for earned wages; 7.13B identify the components of a personal budget, including income; planned savings for college, retirement, and emergencies; taxes; and fixed and variable expenses, and calculate what percentage each category comprises of the total budget; 7.13D use a family budget estimator to determine the minimum household budget and average hourly wage needed for a family to meet its basic needs in the student's city or another large city nearby
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.13A, 7.13B and 7.13D: sales tax, income tax, parts of a budget, budget percents and the hourly wage a family needs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Tax = rate × amount. Budget percent = category ÷ total.
key_sub: $40 with 8.25% tax costs $43.30. $41,600 a year ÷ 2,080 = $20 an hour.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Sales tax is a percent of the price, added at the register. The Texas state rate is 6.25%; cities can add up to 2% more.
  • Income tax is a percent of the money you earn. Texas has no state income tax, but there is federal income tax.
  • A budget lists income, taxes, planned savings (college, retirement, emergencies) and fixed and variable expenses.
  • Category percent = category amount ÷ total budget.

Examples

Example

$40 jeans, 8.25% tax

0.0825 × 40 = $3.30

$40 + $3.30

Answer: $43.30

Example

$41,600 a year needed

41,600 ÷ 2,080

Answer: $20 an hour

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to add the taxTotal = price + tax.
Using the wrong total for a budget percentDivide by the total budget, not another category.
Dividing a yearly amount by 12 for an hourly wageFull time is about 2,080 hours a year: divide by 2,080.

items.q: Why do people save for retirement?
c: Because it is required for school
To have money when they stop working
items.e: Retirement savings pay for life after work.

items.q: Taxes taken from a paycheck are part of which budget item?
items.e: Payroll and income taxes are a budget category.

items.q: Which is a fixed expense?
items.e: A fixed expense is the same every month, like rent.

items.q: Which is a variable expense?
items.e: A variable expense changes from month to month, like groceries.

items.q: Which is usually a fixed expense?
items.e: A phone plan costs the same each month: fixed.

items.q: Why does a budget include an emergency fund?
c: To pay for unexpected costs, like a car repair
items.e: An emergency fund covers surprises without borrowing.

items.q: Which is part of income in a personal budget?
items.e: Income is money coming in, like wages.

items.q: Which is planned savings in a budget?
c: Money set aside each month for emergencies
items.e: Budgets plan savings for emergencies, college and retirement.
